docs.article:
Publish from IFC or USD#

Upload the building model or the USD scene you already have and get a share link where every object can be clicked for its properties and every storey switched off. Nothing to convert on your side.

What to upload#

You haveUploadWhat comes out
A BIM model from Revit, ArchiCAD, Tekla, Allplan, BricsCAD, Bonsai/BlenderBIM…the .ifc file (IFC2x3 or IFC4)one object per product with its GlobalId, IFC type, name, storey and property sets (Pset_*, quantities, type psets)
A USD scene from Omniverse, Houdini, Maya, Blender, Reality Composerone self-contained .usdz (recommended), or a single .usd / .usda / .usdcone object per Mesh prim with its prim path and name, grouped by the Xform below the root; MaterialX (OpenPBR / standard_surface) or UsdPreviewSurface materials and the textures inside the file

Both go through the same door as a GLB: the upload screen (drop the file), POST /v1/ingest (the bytes are recognised; X-Verse-Kind: ifc or usd is optional), or @ctruhtech/verse-sdk:

Code
const { job } = await verse.upload(file, { kind: "ifc", name: "tower-b" });
const rec = await verse.waitForJob(job, { onStage: (s) => console.log(s) });
// rec.url      → the share link
// rec.propsUrl → the object index (per node: id, type, name, storey, props)
// rec.convert  → { kind, schema, products, triangles, materials, storeys, seconds }

The build shows a converting stage with the product count, then the usual prepare → compile → sign → verify ladder. Limits are the ordinary ones (512 MB one-shot, resumable above that); conversion has a 15-minute budget.

In the link#

  • Click an object — the marker names it and the Objects panel opens on its type, storey, id and property sets.
  • Objects panel (the stacked-layers button in the header): a tree by storey, then by type, then product. Tick a storey or a type off to hide it — hidden objects are dropped before the renderer's visibility test, so a hidden floor costs nothing. Isolate keeps only the selected object; Show all restores. Search by name, GlobalId, type or storey.
  • Deep link — Copy link in the panel, or add ?select=<GlobalId> (USD: the prim path) to the share URL; the link opens on that object and orbits onto it.
  • Works in both tiers (WebGPU and WebGL2), in the playground and in embeds.

Embedding#

Code
<div id="model" style="height: 480px"></div>
<script src="https://HOST/embed.js"></script>
<script>
  const v = Verse.embed(document.getElementById("model"), { vpk: "ingest/tower-b-1a2b3c4d5e6f.vpk" });
  v.on("objects", ({ count, storeys, types }) => console.log(count, storeys, types));
  v.on("select", ({ object }) => showPanel(object));          // click → the object's record
  const index = await v.getProperties();                        // the whole index
  const wall = await v.getProperties("2O2Fr$t4X7Zf8NOew3FLOH"); // one object
  v.setVisible(index.storeys.find((s) => s.name === "Level 2").nodes, false);
  v.isolate(index.types.IfcDoor);                               // only the doors
  v.setVisible("all");
  v.select(wall.id, { frame: true });
</script>

The props sidecar is also plain JSON: GET /ingest/<id>.props.json (private scenes: the owner's token or a share token, exactly like the scene). Its shape is documented in docs/api.md → IFC and USD.

Getting a good result#

  • IFC: export with geometry (the "Coordination View" / "Reference View" MVDs are fine) and the property sets you want to see. Spaces, openings, annotations and grids are left out on purpose. Products without a surface style take a palette by type (walls light, slabs grey, doors wood, windows glass) so an unstyled model still reads as a building; styled colours are kept. Large georeferenced models are moved to the origin.
  • USD: pack a .usdz so the textures travel with the layer. References, payloads and sublayers that point at files outside the upload are not followed — flatten the stage first (usdcat --flatten, or export a USDZ). Mesh prims are read with their materials: a MaterialX network (ND_open_pbr_surface_surfaceshader from Blender 4/5, Houdini, Omniverse; ND_standard_surface_surfaceshader from Maya / Arnold) wins over the UsdPreviewSurface written beside it. Base colour, metalness, roughness, normal and emission (with its strength) map to glTF PBR; coat, fuzz / sheen, transmission, specular weight / colour and IOR become the matching KHR_materials_* extensions, which render as listed in what is rendered (clearcoat, sheen, transmission and emission strength on both roads; specular tint in Fidelity mode only — a streamed surface shows its base material there). Separate metallic and roughness textures are packed into one. A Z-up stage is stood upright and metersPerUnit applied (a centimetre stage lands in metres). Not read: skinning, animation, point instancers, subsurface, thin film. Files over 160 MB use the 64-bit converter (the 436 MB Intel Sponza .usda converts in 7 s).
  • The viewer keeps one detail hierarchy per product, so a model with tens of thousands of tiny products streams more roots than a merged mesh would; group furniture or hardware at export time if the first view is slow to settle.
  • Need the lighting baked too? Both inputs end up as ordinary GLB scenes, so Bake for me applies when the file carries lights.

When it does not work#

MessageWhyWhat to do
This file isn't an IFC or USD we can read (bim_invalid)the bytes are not IFC/USD, the IFC has no products with geometry, or the USD has no Mesh primsre-export with geometry; for USD flatten the stage
We couldn't convert this file (convert_failed)the converter crashed or ran past 15 minutestry again; if it repeats, export GLB from your tool and send us the file details
objects without a storeythe IFC does not contain them through IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure (or an aggregate of a contained element)they are listed under No storey in the panel
